subject: Urgent: Elevated 5xx/429 affecting Kyra Health production - action plan & ETA
messages:
From: Elaine Park <elaine@kyrahealth.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-20 15:02 PDT
Subject: High 5xx/429 spike impacting checkout - urgent

Sean —

We’re seeing a sharp increase in 5xx and 429 responses from the Redwood API starting ~14:45 PDT. Impact: several mid-market customers can’t complete payments (checkout timeouts). Sample request IDs attached (kyra_error_samples.txt).

Observed behavior: throughput drops after bursts, then client retries seem to amplify errors. We tried a short restart on our side but saw no improvement. Can you confirm this is on Redwood’s side and provide an ETA for a mitigation?

This is critical for our payment flow — please escalate.

Thanks,
Elaine Park
Head of Platform, Kyra Health
From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@kyrahealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-20 15:20 PDT
Subject: Re: High 5xx/429 spike impacting checkout - urgent

Elaine — thanks for the heads up and for the sample IDs. I’ve opened INC-4283 and looped in our SRE/ops team (Marissa). Initial ask: can you confirm the client retry policy (retries, backoff) and approximate QPS at time of failure?

We’ll triage immediately and will get you an ETA within 30 minutes. I’ll keep this thread for customer comms and we’ll post to the status page once we have a mitigation plan.

Short-term: if you can temporarily reduce retries on the client and ensure exponential backoff, that helps prevent amplification. We’ll follow up with actionable steps.

— Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>, Elaine Park <elaine@kyrahealth.com>
Cc: grace_oconnor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-20 16:05 PDT
Subject: Re: High 5xx/429 spike impacting checkout - urgent

Elaine / Sean — quick triage from the infra side: we see a pattern consistent with retry amplification plus a short-lived routing disruption to the us-west serving pool. Key findings so far:

- Several requests from Kyra’s client burst at T=14:44 with high concurrency and small backoff intervals.
- Our autoscaling reacted but there was a gap while new instances warmed KV caches which caused transient 5xx errors and increased 429 as upstream rate-limits kicked in.

Immediate mitigations I’m pushing now:
1) Apply a temporary rate-limit override for Kyra to smooth bursts (10% headroom)
2) Spin two extra dedicated instances in us-west and pin them to Kyra’s traffic until warm (ETA ~30–40m)
3) Enable fallback routing to a compatible model variant with lower memory footprint to reduce per-request latency (temporary)

Actions for Kyra (please confirm asap):
- Reduce client retries to max 2 with exponential backoff (recommended backoff: base=200ms, multiplier=2).
- If possible, batch small requests for checkout to reduce per-call overhead.

I attached the mitigation runbook (redwood_mitigation_runbook_v2.pdf) with the config snippets.

I’ll update in 30 minutes with scaling progress and ETA for full recovery.

— Marissa
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Elaine Park <elaine@kyrahealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-21 09:12 PDT
Subject: Re: High 5xx/429 spike impacting checkout - urgent

Marissa — thanks. We pushed a quick fix to cap retries and increased client backoff at 17:10 UTC (apologies for the timezone mix). We’re still seeing elevated 429 for a subset of requests and some 5xx intermittently. Traffic profile hasn’t changed much.

Question: will the fallback model materially change output format for our validation or is it a drop-in? We can route a small percentage of requests to fallback if that’s safe. Also, can you confirm if the rate-limit override will be visible on your status page? Our legal/ops team is asking for an ETA because this is affecting live billing windows.

- Elaine
From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@kyrahealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Cc: dylan_brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-21 10:03 PDT
Subject: Re: High 5xx/429 spike impacting checkout - urgent

Elaine — quick update from reliability: we’ve enacted the steps Marissa listed and also initiated two additional measures:

- Rolled traffic for Kyra to the previous model variant (v2.1-stable) as a temporary fallback — it is drop-in for your validation layer, same JSON schema, small difference in tokenization only.
- Manually scaled your dedicated pool by +2 instances in us-west; initialization/warm-up is in progress.

Expectations and ETA: we expect 50% improvement in 429 rate within ~20–30 minutes after warm-up completes; full stabilization targeted within 2 hours. There may be short-lived 5xx during routing changes while caches rehydrate — that’s expected but should be limited.

Status page: Sean, I recommend a short customer-facing note (status.redwood.ai) that we’re investigating elevated error rates for Kyra Health and that mitigation steps are in progress; avoid promising an exact ETA until warm-up completes. I’ll stay on this until errors return to baseline.

— Grace
Director, Reliability Engineering, Redwood Inference
From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@kyrahealth.com>
Cc: dylan_brooks <dylan@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, grace_oconnor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-22 08:50 PDT
Subject: Executive summary & customer-facing next steps

Elaine — following up with an executive summary and next steps. We understand the criticality and have elevated internally. Current status:

- What we observed: retry amplification + transient routing gap causing KV cache warm-up 5xx/429 spike.
- What we did: temporary rate-limit override, +2 dedicated instances in us-west, rolled to v2.1-stable fallback for Kyra traffic.
- Immediate ETA: stabilization in progress; full recovery target 2 hours from now (we will confirm earlier if metrics improve faster).
- Customer-facing step: we’ve posted a short update on our status page (https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-4283) and will keep that updated every 30 minutes while active.

We are open to issuing a one-time usage credit for the impacted window; please let me know if you’d like us to start that process now so it’s ready for your finance team.

I’m keeping Dylan in the loop to align on any executive escalation or customer outreach.

— Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>, Elaine Park <elaine@kyrahealth.com>
Cc: grace_oconnor <grace@redwood.com>, dylan_brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-22 11:49 PDT
Subject: Kyra incident - errors returned to baseline, postmortem draft attached

Elaine / team — final update: observed 5xx/429 rates have returned to baseline ~11:30 PDT after cache warm-up and routing stabilization. Metrics summary: 5xx rate reduced from 3.8% peak to 0.12% baseline; 429s reduced by ~92% vs peak.

Attachments: kyra_incident_postmortem_draft.md (contains timeline, root cause analysis, and permanent mitigations we’ll propose: smarter warm-up prefetching, a more forgiving temporary rate-limit policy for known partners, and an automated routing fallback).

Next steps for Kyra: Marissa will work with your platform team to schedule a follow-up runbook review and a test window to validate the fallback and warm-up changes. We’ll also prepare a short incident brief for billing.

Thanks for your partnership and patience — we’ll send the final postmortem after internal review.

— Marissa Cole
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
